description: Issue #875: BaseCRUDVM.ApplyFileAttachmentResolution used to feed LoadExistingSubItemFileIds' result straight into the sub-item restore-vs-drop decision even when the underlying existing-sub-item lookup QUERY had thrown (a provider parameter cap, a timeout, a transient connection drop, ...). An exception fell through to an empty/partial dictionary, indistinguishable from 'the query succeeded and none of these rejected items match an existing child row'. For a posted ISubFile collection whose every rejected item happened to be the SAME existing child re-posted with an unresolvable FileId -- the ordinary #815 sixth/seventh round scenario -- every item was then dropped instead of restored, emptying the WHOLE posted collection, which routes into DoEditPreparePart2's empty-collection branch: it physically deletes EVERY existing child row for that parent while DoEdit reports success. This is the identical Issue #828 defect, one call site over -- the exhaustive pass Issue #875 required before fixing anything confirmed it, plus a third site (LoadEntitySnapshot/Async) fixed in the same PR. The fix adds a Succeeded flag to LoadExistingSubItemFileIds' result and rejects the WHOLE request when the lookup itself failed -- the identical 'nothing persisted, MSD carries the error' contract Issue #828 already established for the FileAttachment resolution query, reused rather than reinvented. This mutant neutralizes the new guard (`if (!lookup.Succeeded)` -> `if (!lookup.Succeeded && false)`, compile-preserving) in ApplyFileAttachmentResolution, reproducing the exact pre-fix fallthrough with an empty/partial lookup result. Checked against ExistingSubItemLookupFailureGateTests875.cs's DoEdit_ExistingSubItemLookupThrows test, which seeds a Product with ONE pre-existing FileAttachment-backed child, arms a DbCommandInterceptor that throws on every SELECT against the zz_product_attachment table, and re-posts that SAME child's id with an unresolvable (never-seeded) FileId. Under the mutant, the guard never fires, the item is dropped from the posted collection (LoadExistingSubItemFileIds' own lookup never gets a chance to prove a match -- the query throws before it can), emptying the whole collection, DoEditPreparePart2's empty-collection branch deletes the real row, and DoEdit reports success (vm.MSD stays empty) -- exactly what the test's first assertion (the caller must be told the request failed) catches. ApplyFileAttachmentResolution is the ONE method both DoEdit and DoEditAsync route through (via RejectUnresolvableFileAttachmentReferences/Async), so the async counterpart (DoEditAsync_...) hits the identical mutated guard and is listed alongside the sync test as a second red test, not a positive control. The two ACTUAL positive controls -- DoEdit_RejectedCountAboveBatchSize_AllChunksRestore_NoDataLoss (never arms any interceptor) and EntitySnapshotLoadFailureGateTests875's DoEdit_EntitySnapshotLoadThrows_... (arms a DIFFERENT interceptor targeting the unrelated zz_product table, exercising the separate LoadEntitySnapshot Succeeded guard this mutant does not touch) -- both stay green under this mutant, proving its blast radius is exactly the declared line, not the whole fix.
target_symbol: BaseCRUDVM<TModel>.ApplyFileAttachmentResolution(TModel?, List<ScalarFileAttachmentRef>, List<PropertyInfo>, HashSet<Guid>) -- the `if (!lookup.Succeeded)` whole-request-rejection guard for the existing-sub-item lookup, line ~2392

red_expected_assertion_patterns.WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core.Test.VM.ExistingSub: #875: the caller must be told the request failed when the sub-item lookup itself failed
#875 async: the caller must be told the request failed when the sub-item lookup itself failed
